title: Recovering the polyhedral geometry of fragments
author: Török, Domokos

steps.title: Preprocess input data
steps.instruction: Compute the convex hull C(S) of the scanned object S and obtain its triangulated mesh. For each hull face record the vertex coordinates, outward normal vector, and surface area. Calculate the reference point O as the average of all point‑cloud coordinates (O lies inside the hull).

steps.title: Build spherical histogram
steps.instruction: Create a weighted spherical histogram of the hull face normals using a Fibonacci lattice on the unit sphere. Generate an odd number of lattice points P = 2N+1 (e.g., N = 1000 gives P = 2001) with angles θ_i = arccos(2i/(2N+1)) and φ_i = 2π i / φ⁻¹ (φ = (1+√5)/2). For each hull face, find the lattice point whose direction maximises the dot product with the face normal and increase that bin by the face’s surface area. The resulting histogram H(C(S)) is a scalar function on the sphere.

steps.title: Smooth histogram with Gaussian kernel
steps.instruction: Apply Gaussian smoothing to H(C(S)) on the sphere. Use a Gaussian kernel whose distance is the shortest‑path distance on the sphere and vary the standard deviation σ in the range σ ∈ [r/7, r] (r = sphere radius). Increase σ in 50 equidistant steps from 1/7 to 1. Perform this smoothing for the chosen N values (method a: N = 500, 1000, 2000; method b: N = 2000), producing smoothed histograms H(σ).

steps.title: Find local maxima and compute F(σ)
steps.instruction: For each σ‑smoothed histogram, determine the neighbor distance d_nn such that each lattice point has on average six neighbors within d_nn. A bin is a local maximum if its value exceeds that of all its neighbors. Count the number of local maxima; denote this integer‑valued function as F(σ).

steps.title: Determine number of faces
steps.instruction:
Choose the number of faces F of the ideal polyhedron using one of two alternatives:
(a) Identify the longest plateau in the plot of F versus σ and set F to the plateau length (if ambiguous, the second‑longest plateau may be used).
(b) Provide an a‑priori bound Fmax and select the largest value F ≤ Fmax that appears in F(σ).
Note that F may be revised later if the subsequent steps fail.

steps.title: Extract face normals
steps.instruction: Having fixed F, locate the F histogram bins (on the N = 2000 lattice) that correspond to the selected maxima. The unit vectors of these bins are taken as the outward normals of the reconstructed polyhedron faces.

steps.title: Compute face distances from reference point
steps.instruction: For each reconstructed normal n_j, collect hull faces whose normals n_h satisfy n_j·n_h ≥ 0.95 (0.99 gives similar results). Build a weighted distance histogram for this subset using the hull‑face areas as weights. Divide the distance range between the smallest and largest distances into B = 10 equal bins and locate the bin with the maximum count; its centre gives the distance d_j of face j from O. Repeat for all F faces to obtain distances d₁…d_F.

steps.title: Construct hyperplane mosaic and bounded cells
steps.instruction:
Form the set of planes defined by each normal n_j and its distance d_j. Using the algorithm of [1]:
(a) Vertices – solve the linear system for every triple of planes (≈ 16 s(s‑1)(s‑2) combinations) to obtain intersection points.
(b) Edges – group collinear vertices belonging to the same two planes and order them to create edges.
(c) Faces – start from two adjacent edges sharing a vertex, determine the plane, and iteratively add edges that keep the polygon convex and coplanar (select edge with smallest cross‑product magnitude when exact parallelism is absent). Close a loop to store a face; discard open faces.
(d) Polyhedra – assemble faces by linking those that share edges, ensuring exactly three faces meet at each vertex. Identify all bounded cells (convex polyhedra) of the mosaic.

steps.title: Select polyhedron containing reference point
steps.instruction: Among the bounded cells, find the unique cell that contains the reference point O. If no cell contains O, the current set of F planes is invalid; increase F (or adjust σ) and repeat steps 5–8.

steps.title: Remove insignificant faces
steps.instruction: Iteratively evaluate each generated face f_i (i = 1…F). Tentatively delete f_i and recompute the polyhedron volume change dV_i. If dV_i < dv₀ (threshold set to 20 % of the current volume), deem f_i irrelevant and permanently remove it. Continue until no further faces satisfy the removal criterion. The control parameter dv (volume‑increase factor) governs the aggressiveness of this pruning.
